turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): sorry doctor, sorry, we are late only. the metro was completely packed and the auto fellow took a long cut.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): that is quite alright, please sit. it is a hot day to be stuck outside, no?
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): and she wanted chai on the way, doctor. I told her we are late already, but will she listen.
[SEG0004] person_1 (PATIENT): amma, one small cup only. umm. we are here now, that is what matters.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): good. so tell me, what can I do for you today?
[SEG0006] person_1 (PATIENT): well actually, my neighbour aunty caught me yesterday and gave a full lecture, how these hormone tablets spoil the body, and I got a bit uh worked up.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): neighbours have many theories. I want to hear what you yourself have come for.
[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): I want advice on contraception. the wedding is in a few months and I need something I can trust.
[SEG0009] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): she is twenty four, doctor. whole week she is on the phone googling, asking me the same doubt again and again.
[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): amma please. I just have a lot of questions, I don't want to pick a wrong method.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): right. twenty four, wedding coming, you want contraception you can trust, and we will not rush you. have you used any method before?
[SEG0012] person_1 (PATIENT): last year I was on the pill. they called it novolon. one tablet every night, by mouth.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): novolon, one at night by mouth. what made you stop?
[SEG0014] person_1 (PATIENT): headaches. bad ones, like a tight band. they started after maybe two months, or three, I cannot say exactly, and then I just
[SEG0015] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): she stopped it herself doctor. and those days she was finishing disprin from my box, I saw the empty strips.
[SEG0016] person_1 (PATIENT): amma that disprin was yours, I took it two times and left it, it is not my medicine. the headaches went off once I stopped the pill. completely.

[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): right. so headaches on novolon, starting somewhere around two or three months, you cannot pin the time, they cleared after you stopped, and you are not on that pill now. we will leave the disprin, it was your mother's.
[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): yes, that is right. uh also I smoke, but only sometimes. at a party, two or three cigarettes, not daily.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): occasional cigarettes, noted. what about alcohol?

[SEG0020] person_1 (PATIENT): alcohol is just a glass of wine at weddings, not regularly, and I work as a content writer in a small firm in Andheri, hours ten in the morning till eight at night, six days. diet is mostly tiffin from home, rice and dal, and I skip breakfast half the time. exercise, mm I suppose, sometimes, not really, I think of joining a gym and then I don't go.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): thank you, the week is clear to me. any illness in the family, diabetes, pressure, heart problems?

[SEG0022] person_1 (PATIENT): my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar, and my mama, that is my mother's brother, had a heart attack when he was about sixty. uh I think that is everyone.
[SEG0023] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): yes her father was taking tablets for the sugar. I myself have no diabetes, doctor, and my pressure is normal, she is not mixing it up.

[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): let me say it back. father had diabetes, one sister has high blood pressure but not diabetes, your mother's brother had a heart attack. your mother does not have diabetes, so I will not write that as a family illness.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): any allergy to a medicine, or a food, anything you react to?
[SEG0026] person_1 (PATIENT): no. nothing I know of.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): with those pill headaches, before the pain, any flashing lights or zigzag lines in front of the eyes?
[SEG0028] person_1 (PATIENT): mm, I suppose. sometimes, not really. I can't properly remember.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): that is only a maybe, so I will not call it migraine aura. let me check your blood pressure.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): it reads one twenty two over seventy eight. comfortable for you.

[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): okay, good, I was scared it would be high from the smoking. so what can I actually use, will you give the same pill again? I have doubts about an implant also, I saw some photos online.

[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): I would rather not restart a combined pill. you had bad headaches on novolon, and you do smoke, even if only at parties. the choices I can offer are a progesterone only pill, the three monthly injection, a copper device, or the implant in the arm, which lasts three years.
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): the implant, does the fitting pain much? and if I hate it, can you take it out? what if my periods go all irregular, I read that and I am honestly scared.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): fitting is under local anaesthetic, and yes, we can take it out whenever you ask. bleeding may turn irregular or lighter. that is expected, not a sign of harm.

[SEG0035] person_1 (PATIENT): and the copper one, I don't want heavier periods and cramps if that happens. the injection is every three months, no? if I want a baby in two years, will the effect get stuck, I mean stay too long?

[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): a copper device can make periods heavier and more crampy, so if that worries you we can leave it aside. the injection is every twelve weeks, and the return of fertility can be slow, so with the wedding close I would not put it first for you.
[SEG0037] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): then doctor you just finalise the implant, otherwise she will keep asking till night.
[SEG0038] person_1 (PATIENT): amma I need to understand it first. uh doctor, if I take the leaflet home, can the decision be next time? I am not ready today.

[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): yes. I am giving you the implant leaflet now, please read it and write your questions down. come back in two weeks and we will decide together. no prescription from me today.

spec.situation: Young woman asks about contraception, previous pill caused headaches, smokes occasionally; blood pressure read; options discussed; implant leaflet given, decision next visit.

traps.happens: The conversation OPENS with a remark, joke, apology for being late, small talk, or a trigger event (a relative's diagnosis, a neighbour's advice, the receptionist's note) BEFORE the real reason is stated. The patient states the real concern a few turns later.
traps.label_rule: chief_complaint is the real concern in a short phrase in the patient's wording (e.g. 'worried about diabetes', 'voice gets tired'). NOT the opening remark, the joke or the trigger (the relative's illness goes into family_history only if it is a relative's condition said as such).

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

features: interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.

bad.reason: Exercise description supported, but status 'none' is wrong; she says sometimes, not really.
bad.text: exercise (description=Sometimes, not really; thinks of joining a gym but does not go, status=none, reported_by=patient)

bad.reason: Everything supported except certainty 'uncertain'; headache history itself is stated, uncertainty only about exact timing.
bad.text: Headaches (category=neurological, status=resolved, severity=bad, onset=about 2 to 3 months after starting novolon, temporality=past, aggravating_factors=novolon, relieving_factors=stopping novolon, reported_by=patient, certainty=uncertain)

bad.reason: Dose, route, frequency, discontinued status supported; duration and contraception indication not explicitly stated.
bad.text: novolon (dose=1 tablet, route=oral, frequency=every night, duration=approximately 2 to 3 months, indication=contraception, status=discontinued, reported_by=patient)

omissions.text: Headache quality was described as 'like a tight band'.
Patient said the headaches resolved completely after stopping Novolon.

When asked about visual aura before the headaches, the patient gave an equivocal answer ('sometimes, not really, I can't properly remember'), and the doctor explicitly decided not to label it migraine aura.
Family history clarification: mother does not have diabetes, and the doctor explicitly said this would not be recorded as a family illness.
Past medicine mentioned: Disprin was taken only twice from the mother's box during the headache period and was not the patient's regular medicine.
Doctor advised against restarting the combined pill specifically because of headaches on Novolon plus smoking, even if only occasional.
Implant insertion would be done under local anaesthetic.
Doctor said no prescription would be given today.

There was a real difference in preference: the family member wanted the doctor to finalize the implant, but the patient said she was not ready and wanted to decide at the next visit after reading the leaflet.
